diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: Top vertices are CAR_n and CAR_{n+1}; bottom vertices are M_{2^n}(C) and M_{2^{n+1}}(C). The top arrow iota_n has the source/target in the Statement and step 1.1. Vertical arrows pi_n and pi_{n+1} are the faithful occupation matrix isomorphisms from F1, justified by the supplier thm-finite-mode-car-algebra-is-full-matrix-algebra, Statement and proof steps 2.1 and 5.1. The bottom arrow alpha_n sends A to A tensor I_2, of size 2^{n+1} by 2^{n+1}.

diagram_math_checks.relation: pi_{n+1} composed with iota_n equals alpha_n composed with pi_n.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Existing step 1.2 identifies e_S tensor e_epsilon with the subset obtained by appending n+1 exactly when epsilon=1. For j <= n, n+1 never contributes to the count of occupied indices below j in the two toggle formulas of lem-finite-mode-car-occupation-matrix-units. Thus annihilation and creation both act as the n-mode operator tensor I_2. Multiplication and linearity give this square relation for every x in CAR_n. Both horizontal arrows point toward n+1 and both vertical arrows toward matrix algebras.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The last-empty and last-occupied blocks are invariant, and in their grouped order alpha_n(A) has block matrix diag(A,A).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Group F_n tensor e_0 and F_n tensor e_1 after applying the existing occupation identification. The identity on the last bit fixes each summand, so (x_0,x_1) maps to (Ax_0,Ax_1). Explicitly specifying the grouped basis avoids conflating the literal interleaved Kronecker matrix A tensor I_2 with diag(A,A) in a different ordering.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The amplification and therefore iota_n preserve norms, including n=0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Existing step 2.1 bounds the squared output norm by ||A||^2(||x_0||^2+||x_1||^2) and recovers the reverse bound on vectors (x,0). Faithful vertical identifications transfer the equality to CAR_n. For n=0, F_0 has its single empty-set basis vector and the same construction sends scalars to scalar multiples of I_2; no exceptional diagram relation is needed.
